turns.assistant_text:
Here are some notable AI news highlights from today:

1. **The AI industry is picking sides on open or closed tech. Experts say follow the money.** - NBC News discusses how Silicon Valley companies are aligning with either open or closed AI systems, reflecting their business interests. Nvidia has formed an alliance supporting open-weight AI tools, while major players like OpenAI and Anthropic are absent from this initiative. [Read more here.](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/experts-say-money-guiding-ai-industry-debate-open-closed-tech-rcna589495)

2. **5U AI scales up new digital workforce platform** - 5U AI is developing AI Workers that understand freight operations, aiming to enhance logistics workflows. The company is expanding its team to support this growth. [Read more here.](https://www.ajot.com/news/5u-ai-scales-up-new-digital-workforce-platform)

3. **NCTC Aims To Create ‘Easy Button For AI’** - The National Content & Technology Cooperative is preparing to launch a subscription-based AI platform for small and midsize broadband operators, aiming to simplify AI integration in the industry. [Read more here.](https://tvnewscheck.com/ai/article/nctc-aims-to-create-easy-button-for-ai/)

4. **HKT unveils self-developed AI platform HKT.AI** - HKT has launched HKT.AI, a platform designed to provide access to global AI resources, promoting the vision of "AI for All" in Hong Kong. [Read more here.](https://www.voiceofalexandria.com/news/national_business_news/hkt-unveils-self-developed-ai-platform-hkt-ai-one-stop-hub-for-global-ai-resources/article_ffd47d45-4254-5797-8fcb-8e30369bcf71.html)

5. **Microsoft Launches Flurry of AI Security Initiatives to Combat AI-Enabled Threats** - Microsoft has announced new AI security products and initiatives, including Project Perception, aimed at enhancing cybersecurity measures against AI-enabled threats. [Read more here.](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/microsoft-ai-security-initiatives/)

These articles provide a snapshot of the current developments in the AI sector.

items.title: The AI industry is picking sides on open or closed tech. Experts say follow the money. - NBC News
items.summary: IE 11 is not supported. For an optimal experience visit our site on another browser. # The AI industry is picking sides on open or closed tech. Experts say follow the money. Nvidia assembled dozens of companies behind open-source AI days after a hack that scrambled the policy debate. Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif., in 2024.David Paul Morris / Bloomberg via Getty Images file. Add NBC News to Google. As Washington debates how to regulate advanced AI, Silicon Valley companies are increasingly sorting themselves into competing visions of open or closed AI systems. Experts say those positions often reflect something simpler than ideology: their business interests.Top AI chipmaker Nvidia underscored that divide Monday by assembling dozens of companies behind a new alliance supporting open-weight AI tools, while some of the industry’s largest developers of closed-weight AI models, including OpenAI and Anthropic, were notably absent. items.title: 5U AI scales up new digital workforce platform - American Journal of Transportation
items.summary: “We are not building another chatbot that answers questions and disappears, we are building AI Workers that understand freight operations, carry out the work, and capture the reasoning behind every decision, so teams can scale their knowledge as well as their capacity.”. 5U AI works inside existing freight systems and uses multi-agent AI trained for logistics workflows, including the complex exceptions and manual decisions that make forwarding operations difficult to automate with generic AI tools or legacy automation. The company is already live with forwarders and carriers across Europe, including with TCI International Logistics, where its AI Workers are being used across air and ocean freight operations. 5U AI is growing its team as part of the scale-up, with plans to hire across product, engineering, operations, commercial, and customer functions. “AI is one of the most exciting developments logistics has seen for a generation, but its value will depend on people who understand the industry and want to build practical tools that solve real operational problems,” said Abik.

items.title: HKT unveils self-developed AI platform HKT.AI One-stop hub for global AI resources, advancing "AI for All" in Hong Kong - Voice of Alexandria
items.summary: # HKT unveils self-developed AI platform HKT.AI One-stop hub for global AI resources, advancing "AI for All" in Hong Kong. HONG KONG SAR - Media OutReach Newswire - 28 July 2026 - HKT announces the launch of HKT.AI, a one-stop, integrated AI platform that enables businesses and individual customers to access a broad suite of prominent global AI resources through a single and intuitive interface. The platform aims to accelerate the mass adoption of AI in Hong Kong, especially in empowering SMEs in their digital transformation, and advance the vision of "AI for All.". HKT.AI aggregates a wide range of Chinese Mainland-based and global AI resources, enabling businesses and individuals to seamlessly access and switch across specialised applications and tools on a single platform to meet diverse work and everyday needs.

items.title: Microsoft Launches Flurry of AI Security Initiatives to Combat AI-Enabled Threats - Infosecurity Magazine
items.summary: Infosecurity Magazine Home » News » Microsoft Launches Flurry of AI Security Initiatives to Combat AI-Enabled Threats. # Microsoft Launches Flurry of AI Security Initiatives to Combat AI-Enabled Threats. At least that’s what David Weston, corporate VP for AI security at Microsoft told his audience during a Microsoft Security launch preview on July 27. During the event, the Redmond-based company announced a flurry of new AI and security products and initiatives. First, Microsoft launched Project Perception, a new agentic security system designed to help cyber defenders continuously identify, evaluate and reduce security risk. The tech firm also announced the launch of the Microsoft Security Frontier Offensive Research and Generative Exploration (FORGE) Lab. The lab will be led by Team Atlanta,, the group of cybersecurity researchers that won the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency’s (DARPA) AI Cyber Challenge (AIxCC) at DEFCON in the summer 2025, after Microsoft hired the team to head the new initiative, Gallot said.
